claims.text: Consent to the exam: explain the benefits; the patient may accept or decline the evaluation.
claims.quote: Benefits of a sexual assault evaluation are explained, but patients are free to consent to or decline the evaluation.

claims.text: Police: are notified if the patient consents.
claims.quote: The police are notified if patients consent.

claims.text: Before the exam: advise not to wash, shower, douche, change clothes, brush teeth, or use mouthwash, which can destroy evidence.
claims.quote: If patients seek advice before medical evaluation, they are told not to throw out or change clothing, wash, shower, douche, brush their teeth, clip their fingernails, or use mouthwash; doing so may destroy evidence.

claims.text: Evidence timing: evidence weakens after 36 hours but may be collected up to 7 days after the assault, depending on the jurisdiction.
claims.quote: Evidence becomes weaker or disappears as time passes, particularly after > 36 hours; however, depending on the jurisdiction, evidence may be collected up to 7 days after sexual assault.

claims.text: Chain of custody: an identified person must have the evidence at all times.
claims.quote: A chain of custody, in which evidence is in the possession of an identified person at all times, must be maintained.

claims.text: Emergency contraception: levonorgestrel (Plan B One-Step) is sold without a prescription and without age restrictions.
claims.quote: On June 20, 2013, FDA approved PBOS for nonprescription use without age restrictions.

claims.text: EC timing: take as soon as possible, within 72 hours after unprotected sex.
claims.quote: Therefore, FDA recommends that all people using levonorgestrel emergency contraceptives follow the product directions exactly and take the product as soon as possible within 72 hours after unprotected sex or contraceptive failure.

claims.text: HIV PEP: best started within 4 hours; not given after 72 hours.
claims.quote: Prophylaxis for HIV infection is best begun < 4 hours after penetration and should not be given after > 72 hours.

claims.text: Statutory rape: the age of consent varies by state: 16 in most, 17 or 18 in the rest.
claims.quote: As the first column in Table 1 shows, the age of consent varies by state. In the majority of states (34), it is 16 years of age. In the remaining states, the age of consent is either 17 or 18 years old (6 and 11 states, respectively).

claims.text: Reporting a minor's sex: state laws differ widely on whether a minor's sexual activity or statutory rape must be reported as child abuse.
claims.quote: State child abuse reporting laws vary widely in terms of whether or not they require reporting the sexual activity of a minor or statutory rape as child abuse.
